description: ¡Hola a todos! Me llamo Esteban (Evan), soy Tecnólogo Médico en Imagenología y Física Médica , y me desempeño como director del Congreso Científico Escolar  Science Tech Nacimiento, combinando la visión médica, el el liderazgo en divulgación e innovación científica. mi equipo es de nacimiento y somos de una zona rural somos 6 en el equipo.
summary: Another One Lost is built on a core commitment to radical accessibility and equity in STEM education. To ensure no learner is left behind, the platform integrates both Chilean Sign Language (LSCh) and American Sign Language (ASL), empowering deaf and hard-of-hearing students to engage fully with space science. Recognizing the connectivity barriers faced by underserved territories, the game features full offline functionality, bringing high-quality aerospace education directly to rural communities and remote school systems without requiring internet access. Furthermore, its adaptive, intuitive interface and multi-sensory design are specifically crafted to lower cognitive barriers for neurodivergent children, offering a safe, engaging, and structured environment where diverse minds can thrive. By intentionally designing an inclusive, welcoming digital space, the project also actively works to close the gender gap in science, inspiring young girls especially those in rural and underrepresented areas to see themselves as future scientists, engineers, and space explorers. Through these combined innovations, Another One Lost transforms space outreach into a truly universal, barrier-free experience that democratizes aerospace knowledge for every child, regardless of geography, neurotype, or background.
details:
What does it do or how does it work? The player controls an astronaut striving to survive on Mars following an accident. To succeed, they must manage critical resources such as water, oxygen, food, and energy, make high-stakes decisions, and overcome challenges based on real scientific data from NASA. Furthermore, the game incorporates radical accessibility and neurodiversity features so children of all abilities can participate, integrating sign languages (LSCh and ASL), subtitles, visual cues, and an adaptable, clear interface. Crucially, the platform features full offline functionality, allowing it to run smoothly in rural schools and isolated communities without internet access.

What benefits does it offer?

Scientific Education: Teaches about Mars, space weather, radiation, and aerospace exploration using NASA open data.

Inclusion: Enables children with and without disabilities to participate together in the same educational experience.

Logical Thinking & Autonomy: Fosters problem-solving skills, strategic decision-making, and resource management.

Universal Accessibility: Eliminates physical and sensory barriers through Chilean (LSCh) and American (ASL) Sign Language integration.

Social Equity: Promotes equal opportunities, respect for differences, and bridges science gaps for neurodivergent youth and underrepresented girls.

What is the anticipated impact of the project? Our goal is to democratize access to science and technology education, ensuring that no child is ever excluded from space learning due to geography, disability, or neurodivergent conditions. We expect Another One Lost to foster a more inclusive STEM education, ignite early scientific curiosity, and prove that space exploration belongs to everyone.

What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software were used? The development relies on modern open-source web technologies, including HTML5, CSS3, and vanilla JavaScript, hosted seamlessly via GitHub Pages to guarantee high performance and complete offline support. It integrates official NASA scientific data and APIs (such as DONKI, Curiosity/RAD datasets, and OSDR archives) alongside customizable UI components, sign language assets, and accessibility features.

In what way is your project creative? Its creativity lies in seamlessly blending three core pillars: data-driven space exploration, tactical resource management, and radical inclusive accessibility. Unlike conventional educational games, Another One Lost dismantles geographical barriers (operating offline in rural areas) and sensory barriers (via sign language and neuro-inclusive design), enabling players from any background to share a universal scientific adventure.

What factors did your team take into account? Our team carefully considered the following critical factors:

Inclusion & Accessibility: Ensuring active participation for deaf (via LSCh/ASL), blind, and neurodivergent children.

Rural Reach & Connectivity: Implementing a 100% offline-first architecture for remote schools and underserved regions.

Scientific Rigor: Grounding every gameplay mechanic in official open data from NASA.

Gameplay & Fairness: Delivering an engaging, balanced, and intuitive experience that provides equal opportunities for all learners.
